correctness.rationale: Commuting normality and the row bound give an abelian spectral model with essential range in a bounded ell2 ball, so B_lambda=strong-sum (T_j-lambda_j)^*(T_j-lambda_j) is multiplication by ||z-lambda||². CAR anticommutation supplies the degreewise Laplacian dd*+d*d=B_lambda⊗I; independently tested this identity and nilpotence for a small normal-diagonal finite tuple. For lambda off spectral support, B_lambda≥delta²I, and the exact contracting preimage B_lambda^-1 d* has norm at most delta^-1; degree-zero Moore–Penrose minimum preimages attain the same operator norm. At lambda in support, a nonzero kernel of B_lambda yields infinite harmonic homology in every positive exterior degree, or else d1 has dense nonclosed range and infinite algebraic quotient dimension, so infinite-degree Fredholmness fails. Approximate joint eigenvectors yield d_H(K_T,K_S)≤column norm; scalar tuples attain coefficient 1. The noncompact example T_j=projection onto e_j has K={e_j}, showing why norm-summability must not be inferred.
